reasoning: Within the last 45 days, the only true general‑election polling we have for Idaho’s 2026 Senate race is a Peak Insights poll reported via Election Time on X, showing Republican Sen. Jim Risch leading independent Todd Achilles by 34 points, which points to an overwhelming Republican advantage in the Senate race.[1] Another write‑up referencing a June Peak Insights poll similarly shows Risch with a dominant lead over Democratic and minor‑party opponents, and prediction‑market and modeling coverage from Octagon all frame the race as one where Risch is overwhelmingly favored, consistent with Idaho’s strongly Republican Cook PVI.[4][12][10] There is no recent, state‑specific presidential general‑election polling in the results provided, so the current numeric margin can only be stated for the Senate race, which is safely R+ in the mid‑30s; the structural PVI remains strongly R‑leaning statewide.[1][4][10][12]

sources.name: Peak Insights via Election Time (X)
sources.details: Peak Insights statewide poll, as relayed by Election Time on X, finds Jim Risch at 52% and Todd Achilles at 18% among 500 likely voters in Idaho’s 2026 Senate race, a 34‑point Republican lead.

sources.name: PredictionHunt (reporting Peak Insights poll)
sources.details: PredictionHunt summary of a June 2026 Peak Insights Idaho Senate poll reports Risch at 55%, Democrat David Roth at 15%, independent Todd Achilles at 7%, and other minor candidates in single digits, implying an extremely large Republican lead over the main opponents.

sources.name: Octagon Idaho Senate Winner Market/Model
sources.details: Octagon’s Idaho Senate winner prediction market/model places Jim Risch around 94% to win, with Roth at about 2% and Achilles near 5%, describing Risch as benefiting from strong Republican support in a conservative state.

sources.name: NBC News Idaho Senate Primary 2026 Results
sources.details: NBC News’ Idaho Senate primary 2026 live results show Risch winning the Republican primary comfortably and Roth winning the Democratic primary, providing procedural confirmation of the major‑party nominees but no general‑election margin.

sources.name: Idaho Capital Sun
sources.details: Idaho Capital Sun reports that Democratic Senate candidate David Roth ended his campaign for the U.S. Senate seat held by Jim Risch, highlighting Democratic recruitment and continuity challenges but not providing polling numbers.

sources.name: Polymarket Idaho Senate Margin Markets
sources.details: Polymarket’s Idaho Senate margin of victory markets show the leading pricing focused on Republican victory buckets in the 20–25% and 25–30% range, indicating traders expect a comfortable Republican win but not providing a single firm margin.

sources.name: Politically.com (Bullfinch Group/VoteHub listing)
sources.details: Politically.com lists an Idaho 2026 poll attributed to The Bullfinch Group via VoteHub with Risch at 34% and Achilles at 30%, but without full context or methodology and with figures that conflict with better‑documented Peak Insights polling.

sources.details: Polymarket’s ID‑01 House margin of victory market notes that Idaho’s 1st congressional district has a Cook PVI of R+22 and Trump +45 in 2024, speaking to Idaho’s broader Republican lean but not directly to the statewide 2026 Senate or presidential races.
